items.titleEn: Gold will reach $4,600/oz by Q4 2027 as rates fall, USD gives back 10% overvaluation – J.P. Morgan's Tang
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold prices will likely remain under pressure in the near term as monetary policy continues to tighten, but central bank purchases and demand for the precious metal as a hedge against currency debasement will support gold over the medium term, with prices reaching $4600 by year-end 2027, according to Yuxuan Tang, strategist at J.P. Morgan. “I think over the near term it's going to be tough, because it's not the best environment for gold in a rising yield environment,” she said in a recent interview with CNBC. “And I'm not talking about the day-to-day moves in Treasuries. It's the overall monetary tightening backdrop that is adding pressure to gold.” However, Tang said that conditions will become more favorable for gold in the second half of the coming year.

items.titleEn: What's driving SanDisk stock higher today?
items.summaryEn: Buy SNDK. The Nvidia GB200 rack demo shows AI can use far more NAND via SSD “memory expansion,” and SanDisk already has Kioxia JV coverage through 2034 plus accelerating data-center revenue (+61% QoQ) with fiscal Q2 revenue guidance ($12.2B+). The stock is deeply off YTD highs, so any sustained shipment/margin confirmation can re-rate the name quickly. Key Risk: NAND prices fall hard enough that higher volumes don’t translate into profit growth (margin compression wipes out the earnings rebound). Buy Micron (MU) as a higher-beta way to play the same NAND demand theme. If AI servers truly need more SSD-backed flash capacity, the whole NAND supply chain benefits, and MU is positioned to capture incremental pricing/volume as data-center builds expand.

items.titleEn: Micron, SK Hynix, SanDisk stocks rise but what's the verdict on demand outlook?
items.summaryEn: Buy MU. The article flags oversupply risk, but also notes supply may stay tight into 2028 because capacity is being steered toward AI-focused HBM and manufacturers can cut production to defend LTA pricing. With MU down >35% in a month, the market is pricing a worse demand collapse than the base-case implies; the rebound signals buyers are already positioning for a “not-quite-glut” outcome. Key Risk: Data-center permitting delays turn into a real demand break and prices roll over faster than manufacturers can cut supply. Buy SK Hynix. It’s up ~6% on the day while the core debate is whether AI infrastructure spending persists. Hynix is better positioned than pure-play conventional DRAM because AI systems pull more HBM, and the article explicitly says capacity allocation toward AI can keep conventional supply constrained. If AI capex holds, Hynix should outperform as the market reprices “tight supply longer.”

items.titleEn: Why are CoreWeave and Nebius stocks soaring despite mounting debt risks?
items.summaryEn: Buy CRWV. The key catalyst is a $4.5B Meta-linked loan at ~7–7.5% secured by GPUs and tied to Meta demand—far cheaper than ~18% bond yields. That signals lenders believe cash flows are contract-backed, and it can quickly reduce near-term refinancing stress. The stock’s rebound after heavy shorting also gives upside momentum if the market starts pricing the cheaper funding path. Key Risk: The loan terms fall apart or Meta-linked collateral doesn’t translate into real repayment coverage, forcing CRWV back into high-cost refinancing. Buy NBIS. Management expects $17–$20B of customer prepayments in 2027 plus contract-backed borrowing to cover most of $40–$45B capex, leaving a smaller funding gap. With a cash cushion (~$7.4B), the market can re-rate NBIS if investors believe prepayments are durable and not delayed.

items.titleEn: Micron stock is highly undervalued as the Wyckoff Theory takes shape
items.summaryEn: Buy MU. The article flags extreme valuation (forward P/E ~3.4 vs sector ~18) alongside strong fundamentals (gross margin ~87%, revenue growth accelerating, Q1 ~$61B and Q2 ~$66B). The Wyckoff “markdown” setup implies forced selling, which often creates a tradable overshoot below intrinsic value. Catalyst: the $35B buyback starting in December after restrictions end, which should mechanically support EPS and reduce float. Key Risk: The memory upcycle breaks—DRAM demand and pricing fall faster than revenue guidance, making the “cheap” valuation stay cheap. Sell short the memory-exposed peer basket (e.g., short Samsung ADR via SSNLF and/or SK hynix ADR via HXSY) against MU. If the AI/data-center financing fears and “memory supercycle” end risk hit the group, weaker balance sheets and more fragile pricing power should underperform MU. This trade monetizes second-order contagion from AI funding stress into broader memory supply/demand expectations while keeping MU as the relative-value winner on buybacks and valuation.

items.titleEn: Missed the Anthropic IPO? Is now a better time to buy the stock?
items.summaryEn: Buy NASDAQ:ANT. The sell-off looks more valuation- and spending-fear driven than demand-fear: revenue run-rate is accelerating (annualised ~$81B) and losses are narrowing (adjusted operating income positive). Canaccord’s Buy/$135 and the market’s rebound above IPO price suggest momentum is returning, and the stock is still priced off huge growth (29x 2026 revenue) rather than collapsing fundamentals. Key risk: customer demand fails to keep pace with contracted compute, forcing margin compression and renewed “overbuilt capacity” fears. Key Risk: Customer spending doesn’t justify the contracted compute, crushing margins and re-triggering the valuation sell-off. Sell short NASDAQ:NVDA (or reduce exposure via a put on NVDA). If ANT’s thesis hinges on whether future spending matches capacity, the second-order effect is that AI capex growth becomes more lumpy and price-sensitive: hyperscalers and AI labs may delay incremental GPU purchases when utilization risk rises. That hits the “picks-and-shovels” demand multiple even if the long-term AI story stays intact. Key risk: a broad AI capex acceleration overrides utilization fears and NVDA demand stays strong despite ANT-specific concerns.

items.titleEn: AMD, Intel, Broadcom rally in premarket trading Friday as AI stocks rebound
items.summaryEn: Buy AMD. The news adds real AI-infrastructure demand support (TensorWave’s 6-year OpenAI deal) plus AMD’s AI stack buildout (World Labs + Taalas) and a likely sentiment tailwind from the broader chip rebound. If AI capex stays firm, AMD should keep gaining share in data-center compute and inference. Key Risk: AI infrastructure spending slows or gets delayed, making AMD’s growth narrative break. Buy Broadcom. The Anthropic financing structure ($63B) is a direct, funded path for Broadcom’s custom AI accelerators and networking equipment—stronger than a generic “AI rebound.” If the deal converts into sustained shipments, earnings durability improves ahead of the Dec 9 results.

items.titleEn: Is Nvidia stock Wall Street's biggest Black Friday bargain?
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. It’s trading ~9x next-year earnings versus ~17x Broadcom and ~27x AMD, while data-center revenue is still surging (+110%) and management guides strong fiscal 2028 growth (~75%). Huang’s return also directly reduces near-term execution fears (supplier/product/retention). Upside case is simple: if earnings land near consensus and the multiple normalizes toward ~15x, the stock can re-rate sharply. Key Risk: Earnings miss (especially fiscal 2028) and the market refuses to pay a higher multiple, turning the “discount” into a value trap. Buy AMD. The article highlights NVDA’s relative cheapness, but AMD’s forward multiple (~26.9x) implies the market is already pricing in a lot of success. If AI demand stays broad and NVDA’s re-rating lifts the whole AI compute complex, AMD can benefit from multiple expansion even without matching NVDA’s growth rate.

items.titleEn: Adidas, Puma stocks fall as JPMorgan downgrades both on 2027 outlook
items.summaryEn: Buy Adidas. JPMorgan’s downgrade is based on “limited scope for further gains” and fear that 2027 growth targets are hard to hit, but the company just delivered reassuring profit and sales (net profit €706m; operating profit €1.01b) and maintained strong 2026 guidance. The market is overreacting to a 2027 narrative while near-term fundamentals are improving, especially in apparel and DTC. Key upside catalyst: if Stan Smith and running franchises (Hyperboost/Supernova) show franchise expansion, the stock can re-rate quickly from a lowered target. Key Risk: 2027 franchise scaling fails and Adidas needs heavy promotions, compressing margins and forcing guidance cuts. Sell Puma. The downgrade to Underweight plus a lower target (€21 from €26) signals investors won’t pay for inventory progress alone. Inventories are down, but the core issue is “how quickly” Puma can return to growth amid intensifying competition. If sales momentum doesn’t re-accelerate, the market will treat restructuring as a one-off benefit and keep the multiple depressed.

items.titleEn: SpaceX stock surges 7.5%: could Elon Musk's giveaway spark a bigger rally?
items.summaryEn: Buy NASDAQ:SPCX. The giveaway is a catalyst for a durable retail shareholder base, and the market is already repricing toward a higher “ownership + growth” narrative. Pair that with concrete fundamentals: FCC approval for up to 1M satellites for Starmind and continued AI infrastructure buildout. Jefferies’ Buy/$210 and the stock still below the $135 IPO reference make the setup asymmetric if sentiment holds. Key Risk: A sharp drop in SpaceX’s share price that makes the giveaway look like a value-transfer/dilution story, crushing retail demand and momentum. Buy a 3–6 month bull call spread on NASDAQ:SPCX (e.g., buy the 1–2 strike above spot, sell a higher strike). This monetizes the near-term rally from the giveaway headlines while keeping downside limited if the stock mean-reverts after the initial pop. The second leg is that retail flows typically persist for weeks after a high-visibility pledge, not just overnight.

items.titleEn: Samsung, SK Hynix stocks surge: why smart money sees a buying opportunity
items.summaryEn: Buy. The sell-off is extreme versus fundamentals: ~2.01x projected 2027 earnings, with operating profit still massive. The thesis is supported by concrete demand protection—SK Hynix has long-term agreements covering >50% of capacity for 2027–2028 and is pushing HBM4 to mainstream this quarter. Add the catalyst of large shareholder returns (~100T won planned), which should attract “value + yield” buyers if memory sentiment stabilizes. Key Risk: A prolonged memory oversupply that forces HBM and DRAM pricing down enough to break the 2027 earnings assumptions. Buy. Valuation is also deeply compressed (~2.29x projected 2027 earnings) after a >50% drawdown, and the article flags capitulation-style selling with foreign inflows returning. The setup is a re-rating trade: if memory pricing merely stops deteriorating, Samsung’s earnings power and the expectation of further shareholder-return details in January can pull the stock back toward “cheap but improving” rather than “cheap and falling.”

items.titleEn: Stephen Yiu explains why Nvidia stock isn't out of the woods just yet
items.summaryEn: Buy/hold NVDA. The article says underlying sales are surging (fiscal Q3 revenue $115.8B, +103% YoY) and the market may already be pricing the leadership shock. The key near-term catalyst is whether congressional/investigation disclosures actually damage Nvidia’s controls and chip distribution—until then, the “negative” AA watch is a risk premium, not a confirmed earnings hit. Key Risk: A new disclosure ties governance/control failures directly to Nvidia’s business practices (not just leadership), leading to real revenue/China-distribution constraints or major penalties. Sell/trim NVDA into any “AA− within 90 days” narrative. If governance concerns persist, S&P can downgrade to AA−, which typically pressures institutional holders and raises funding/credit-linked risk appetite. Use this as a tactical reduction while waiting for Dec. 1–2 interviews to clarify whether scrutiny reaches Nvidia’s operations.

items.titleEn: SAP shares outlook as it plots another 10,000 round of layoffs: buy or sell?
items.summaryEn: Buy SAP (SAP SE). The news is bad optics, but the fundamentals are improving: cloud backlog +28% to €24B and cloud ERP revenue +29% to €5.96B. Layoffs are a profitability lever while AI spend ramps, and the stock is already bouncing hard after the dip—suggesting investors are willing to pay for the turnaround. Key risk: SAP’s cost cuts fail to translate into sustained margin expansion, and the market re-rates the stock lower because the valuation (forward P/E ~27) is too rich for the growth/margin profile. Sell a basket proxy for high-multiple enterprise software: short ServiceNow (NOW) and Workday (WDAY) versus long SAP (pair trade). If SAP’s layoffs are the “AI efficiency” template, the second-order effect is that investors will demand the same margin proof from peers—compressing multiples across the group, especially the most expensive names. SAP’s backlog growth gives it relative staying power, while NOW/WDAY have less visible near-term cost-to-profit leverage. Key risk: peers deliver stronger-than-expected AI-driven growth and margins, and the market lifts multiples instead of compressing them. Key Risk: Peers beat on AI growth/margins, and multiples expand instead of compressing.
